SEP — DEC 2026BASTROP, TEXASThe Boring CompanySoftware Engineering InternWorking across six internal engineering and operations tools.

Software that meets the physical world.

I build and debug interfaces, backend services, and data workflows used by operational teams. The work means following failures across service, database, container, and network boundaries, then checking that a fix holds end to end.

  • Contributing across six internal engineering and operations tools: React/TypeScript interfaces, Django services, PostgreSQL workflows, and Dockerized applications used by operational teams.
  • Implementing backend and infrastructure improvements with Kubernetes, server-side Redis caching, AWS/S3 data pipelines, and Linux/Nginx deployments, and tracing failures across application, service, database, and network boundaries.
  • Working directly with internal users and engineers to turn loosely scoped operational problems into production changes, balancing reliability, maintainability, and speed.
  • Built an internal engineering knowledge layer using a Grok-based bot.

React · TypeScript · Django · PostgreSQL · Kubernetes · Redis · AWS/S3 · Docker · Linux · Nginx

MAY — AUG 2026NEW YORK, NEW YORKHyphenateFORMERLY MAXIMOR AISoftware Engineering InternTook Flux Analysis from a static prototype to three enterprise customers.

From an AI feature to enterprise software.

My work spanned product scoping, frontend workflows, backend services, data integration, validation, and rollout. I rebuilt a single-call LLM feature into a managed-agent system and worked on the financial-data foundations beneath it.

  • Took Flux Analysis from a static pre-production prototype to deployment across three enterprise customers in the roughly $10M–$100M revenue range, owning scoping, architecture, implementation, testing, rollout, and iteration.
  • Rebuilt Flux from a single LLM call into a managed-agent system using the Claude SDK, with customer-context RAG, backend tool integration, human review, and Temporal orchestration for multi-step analysis and retries.
  • Translated distinct customer accounting structures and reporting workflows into reusable product behavior across FastAPI, React/TypeScript, NetSuite, Snowflake, and PostgreSQL, rather than one-off implementations.
  • Built a validation harness against independent NetSuite SuiteQL queries and drove line-item correctness to 99%; debugged duplicate, stale, and soft-deleted records across production financial-data pipelines.
  • Configured reproducible DevPod environments on AWS ECS/Fargate for five engineers, and migrated integration endpoints from Flask to FastAPI with typed schemas, auth, validation, tests, and explicit failure handling.

Claude SDK · RAG · Temporal · FastAPI · React/TypeScript · NetSuite · Snowflake · PostgreSQL · AWS ECS/Fargate

JAN 2026 — PRESENTCHAMPAIGN, ILLINOISParasol Lab, UIUCResearch Assistant · Parallel ComputingStudying parallel numerical algorithms, scalability, and memory behavior.

What changes when the work runs in parallel?

I work with C++ and the STAPL framework on parallel scan, reduction, and inner-product primitives. The research connects algorithmic reasoning with the behavior of real multithreaded workloads.

  • Implementing parallel scan, reduction, and inner-product primitives in C++/STAPL.
  • Profiling synchronization, memory-access behavior, load balancing, and scalability across multithreaded workloads.
  • Comparing parallel primitives with sequential baselines to understand bottlenecks.

C++ · STAPL · Parallel computing · Benchmarking

05 / THE PERSON BEHIND THE SYSTEMS

I like the part
where the abstraction
meets reality.

I study Computer Science and Economics at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, with a minor in Mathematics (GPA 3.87/4.00). I expect to graduate in May 2028. I’m interested in how software changes the decisions people can make, whether they’re reviewing financial results or working with physical machines.

At Hyphenate, that meant turning AI-enabled accounting workflows into something teams could use. At The Boring Company, it means learning systems by tracing how they behave end to end.

I’m also building Zaap AI, a personal-finance product for students and young professionals. The goal: make understanding your money more accessible.

THE 60-SECOND VERSION

I connect the pieces.

I’m Siddhant Shankar, a CS + Economics student at UIUC and a Software Engineering Intern at The Boring Company.

  1. AI that becomes a product.

    At Hyphenate, I rebuilt Flux Analysis from a single LLM call into a managed-agent system (Claude SDK, RAG, human review, Temporal orchestration). Three enterprise customers in the $10M–$100M revenue range adopted it in three months.

  2. Data people can trust.

    I investigated duplicate and stale financial records across a multi-system pipeline and implemented deterministic deduplication.

  3. Systems understood end to end.

    In my first week at The Boring Company, I traced a missing telemetry signal to an allowlist and confirmed the signal in the application.

Beyond those stories: I founded Zaap AI (50 beta users), research parallel algorithms at Parasol Lab, led the AutoDock simulation team, taught as a UIUC Course Assistant, and worked in product evaluation at Zeus Learning and financial-data engineering at APAC.
